newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha springs higher on crude, end-users.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha springs higher on crude, end-users.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices sprung higher on Wednesday after crude oil spiralled up and end-users appeared to be stepping up their buying interest for February, traders said.

The market would have been more active if not for the continued high freight rates in the north and in the Med, but some appeared interested in loading together cargoes to optimize those rates, they said.
Feb swaps rose about $4 to $223/$223.50 a tonne, with deals heard done both above and below there. Cargoes were still commanding a premium to that of about $1-$3.
"Physically it still looks well supplied," said one NWE broker. "There is (end-user) interest but it's mostly (private and confidential)."
He said some Russian material was placed on Tuesday and there was none currently available in NWE.
In the Med, two to three cargoes each of Skikda and Alexandria, of about 30,000 to 40,000 tonnes, were seen available, as well as some Russian pieces, an Italian trader said.
"There are still volumes available," he said.
He said the high freight rates were pushing the spread between CIF and FOB prices out toward $17-$18, and would narrow as soon as the shipping conundrum was worked out.
Naphtha's rich price relative to gasoline was also squashing reformer demand for the high naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) material, he said.
